\label{lemma-locally-finite-nr-irred-local-fppf}
The property $\mathcal{P}(S) =$``every quasi-compact open of $S$
has a finite number of irreducible components'' is local
in the fppf topology.
statement: Fix a nonnegative integer $k$ when the named property involves $(S_k)$ or $(R_k)$. Let $S$ be a scheme. The property "every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components" (meaning each quasi-compact open subset of the scheme has only finitely many irreducible topological components) is local for the fppf topology: for every fppf covering $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, the scheme $S$ has this property if and only if every member $S_i$ has it.
hypotheses: S is a scheme; k is fixed when relevant; {S_i→S} is a fppf covering.
conclusions: The property "every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components" holds on S exactly when it holds on all covering schemes S_i.
